provenance.provenance_evidence: The project-owned projection passage reproduces the retained calendar body hash exactly. Its artifact manifest records the bounded public-domain 1862 Pustet antecedent, the separate 1962 target, and every editorial transformation; neither witness is represented as owning the projected bytes. The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 sets no comma after 'quaesumus'; 1862 conclusion is the LONGER 'Per Dominum nostrum.'; the 1962 prints the short cue 'Per Dominum.' The expansion runs the other way here from the usual case. Corroboration: 1604 text-layer lines 20453-20458 prints the whole Collect, 'Concede quaesumus omnipotens Deus: vt qui ex merito nostrae actionis affligimur, tuae gratiae consolatione respiremus. Per Dominum nostrum.', with 'nostrae actionis affligimur' legible at 20456. Degraded-latin witness, corroboration only.. Recorded limitation: The 1862 layer reads 'nostra' for 'nostrae' at line 24874 ('ex merito nostra actionis'), which is the characteristic loss of the ae ligature but is also a grammatical difference on its face, so I am not treating it as a mere accent artifact; it also reads 'onim-potens' for 'omnipotens' at 24872-24873. I inferred those letterforms rather than read them; 'nostrae actionis' is printed at the same place in the 1604 at line 20456. All 1862 readings here rest on the tracked whole-book text layer alone; no page image of the 1862 is available to this lane and none was read.
